## Summary

P05.1 implements the **probabilistic top of the resolution cascade** — the §14.7 quality gates everything downstream depends on. Following the P03.2 pattern (and because connectors/ER are not DB-wired yet), it ships as pure, tested library code plus versioned TOML data; the review-queue persistence and curation UI are P05.2.

- **Splink 4 on DuckDB** (SIG-IDENT-021) driven as a **fully-specified, deterministic** model — per-level m/u in versioned data — so the Fellegi–Sunter match weight and its per-comparison Bayes-factor decomposition are reproducible and explainable (SIG-IDENT-025), never EM-trained.
- **Tiers 4 (probabilistic) and 5 (weak-signal)** create `PROPOSED` proposals routed to review and **never auto-write**; tier 6 persists **no per-pair record** (SIG-IDENT-020).
- **Sized blocking** rejected above a documented ceiling; suffix-alone / state-alone prohibited; **trigram is candidate-search only, never a decision score** (SIG-IDENT-023, SIG-IDENT-024).
- **Gold set**: stratified blocked-pair sampling across weight bands, double adjudication with Cohen's κ, a three-value label vocabulary, written rules, per-label provenance, and a **frozen, immutable holdout** (SIG-IDENT-027).
- **Quality gates**: pairwise P/R/F1 at each tier boundary + B-cubed cluster P/R on the holdout; **auto-write tiers demoted to review on a holdout-precision breach**; **cluster-shape alerts** for the bad-merge signatures — oversized PD/sheriff clusters and single-bridge joins of substantial components (SIG-IDENT-028, SIG-IDENT-029).
- **ER as a distinct, re-runnable pipeline stage** between `normalize()` and `load()` with its own run record, quality report, and rollback; a re-cluster emits **new `same_as` under a new ruleset version without destroying the prior clustering**; cluster-shape changes are routed through the public-identifier **stability contract** (SIG-RECON-001, SIG-RECON-002, SIG-IDENT-032).

Implements spec: `docs/tickets/P05.1__probabilistic-er.md` (§14.6–14.8, §27). ADR-029 records the Splink decision (the spec's logical Appendix-F "ADR-016"; repo ADR-016 was already Dagster).

## What changed

- **New modules** (`resolution/src/resolution/`): `blocking.py`, `probabilistic.py`, `gold_set.py`, `quality_gates.py`, `er_run.py`.
- **New versioned data** (`resolution/src/resolution/data/`): `blocking_rules.toml`, `splink_model.toml`, `gold_set_rules.toml`, `quality_gates.toml`.
- **Edited**: `cascade.py` (docstring accuracy only — tiers 0–3 behaviour unchanged, back-compat), `cli.py` (`er-match`, `block-size` subcommands), `__init__.py`, `resolution/pyproject.toml` (+`splink>=4`, +`duckdb`), root `pyproject.toml` (mypy overrides for the new heavy stubs), `uv.lock`, `pylock.toml`.
- **Docs**: `docs/adr/ADR-029-...md` (+ index), `docs/traceability.md`, `docs/risk_register.md`.
- **Tests** (`tests/resolution/`): `test_blocking.py`, `test_probabilistic.py`, `test_gold_set.py`, `test_quality_gates.py`, `test_er_run.py`, `test_cli_er.py` (86 new tests).

## Design decisions

- **Deterministic model, not trained** — a learned/EM model would be non-deterministic and undefendable as a stated rule (§28.1); fully-specified m/u gives the same math with reproducible, explainable output. The gold set + holdout + demotion gate bound the risk of a mis-specified model.
- **Pure library, no DB write path** — like the connectors (ADR-026/027/028), the stage produces `PROPOSED` proposals, `same_as` relations, and a run record as value objects with `to_row()` shapes; wiring to the claim/resolution tables + review queue is P05.2/P08.x.
- **Deterministic pass excludes the trigram rule** — trigram is a probabilistic candidate-search aid (SIG-IDENT-024), so the deterministic tiers do not depend on trigram sizing.

## Verification

- `make check` green: ruff lint + format, mypy (104 source files), full `pytest` (1001 items), and the generated-artifact gate (`pylock.toml` + ontology) — CI-green incl. the phase gate (§51.3).
- 86 new tests; full non-DB suite 959 → 1001 with DB tests. No regressions.
- **Live-driven** (CLI console script + gate scripts): `er-match` scores near-duplicates as tier 4 and a genuinely-different San Diego/San Francisco pair as a weak tier 5, all `PROPOSED`/review; `block-size` rejects state-alone (SIG-IDENT-023); tier-boundary precision drops as a non-match is admitted; B-cubed penalises a seeded bad merge; a tier-2 precision breach demotes to review; oversized-LE and single-bridge alerts fire; a re-cluster merge redirects the retired id to a preserved survivor.
